topic: Ribosomes, Cytoskeleton, Cilia, Flagella and Centrosome
title: How Do Cell Hairs Sweep Dust? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Aarav caught a cold, and his doctor said tiny hairs on the cells of his windpipe sweep mucus and dust up and out. Aarav asks: how can a hair on a single cell move at all? The answer is a skeleton of protein tubes inside the cell, and the ribosomes that build those proteins.

You will see ribosomes (80S = 60S + 40S, 70S = 50S + 30S, the Svedberg unit), then a zoom ladder from the cytoskeleton to cilia, one cilium and its 9 + 2 axoneme with radial spokes and linkers. Watch cilia beat with a stroke and a return, in a wave that moves mucus, and a flagellum push a cell. Then the centrosome, the cartwheel of a centriole with nine triplets and a hub, cilia vs flagella side by side, a pause and think, six ribosomes sorted, the 100S exam trap, an original NEET-pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions.

This is Episode 66 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
